facts.statement: The genus Antarctilamna was described by Young in 1982.
The genus includes two species: Antarctilamna prisca and Antarctilamna ultima.
facts.quote: subdivision: Antarctilamna prisca Young 1982 Antarctilamna ultima Gess and Coates 2015

facts.statement: Antarctilamna is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish that lived during the Devonian period.
facts.quote: Antarctilamna is an extinct genus of Devonian cartilaginous fish originally exemplified by Antarctilamna prisca from South Eastern Australia and Antarctica.

facts.statement: The most recently occurring species, Antarctilamna ultima, was found at the Waterloo Farm lagerstätte in South Africa.
facts.quote: The latest occurring described species is Antarctilamna ultima from the Waterloo Farm lagerstätte in South Africa.

facts.statement: Antarctilamna possessed robust spines located in front of the first dorsal fin that lacked a deep insertion area.
facts.quote: Antarctilamna has robust ctenacanthid-like spines which lack a deep insertion area, and are borne in front of the first dorsal fin

facts.statement: The fish had distinctive diplodont teeth featuring small intermediate cusps.
facts.quote: in addition to distinctive diplodont teeth with small intermediate cusps

facts.statement: Fossils of Antarctilamna have been discovered in Antarctica and Australia.
facts.quote: Fossils of Antarctilamna have been found in Antarctica and Australia.

facts.statement: The description of Antarctilamna prisca is based on material from both Antarctic and New South Wales localities.
facts.quote: The description of Antarctilamna prisca includes material derived from both Antarctic and New South Wales localities

facts.statement: Antarctilamna ultima is described from an individual approximately 1 meter long.
facts.quote: It is described from an assemblage of elements including a dorsal fin spine, jaws and diplodont teeth derived from an individual that was approximately 1m long.

facts.statement: Estimates suggest Antarctilamna ultima could have reached several meters in length.
facts.quote: A rough estimate assuming a constant relationship between tooth width, mandibular length and body length suggests that Antarctilamna ultima reached several metres in length.

facts.statement: Antarctilamna ultima is the first recorded Devonian cartilaginous fish known from a juvenile specimen.
facts.quote: Antarctilamna ultima is the first recorded Devonian chondrichthyan known from a juvenile specimen

facts.statement: The juvenile status of Antarctilamna ultima is supported by its small size and a head and branchial region exceeding a quarter of its body length.
facts.quote: the latter's juvenile status is supported not just by its extremely small size, but also by its very large head and branchial region, which together exceeded a quarter of its body length.

facts.statement: Studies suggest large sharks may have entered the Waterloo Farm estuary to forage, though it is also possible they gave birth there, using the lake as a nursery.
facts.quote: Studies suggests that large sharks frequently entered the Waterloo Farm estuary from the sea when the mouth was open, in order to forage, but it is also possible that they gave birth within the estuarine lake which acted as a nursery area for these species.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Antarctilamna is related to xenacanths or represents a basal chondrichthyan.
facts.quote: Authors have either suggested that Antarctilamna is related to xenacanths, or that it is a basal chondrichthyan.

facts.statement: The parent group of Antarctilamna is the family Antarctilamnidae.
Antarctilamna belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
Antarctilamna lived from the Lochkovian to the Famennian stages, between 419.62 and 358.86 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lochkovian to Famennian (419.62 to 358.86 million years ago)
